title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 66-69). Grothendieck is axiomatising a 'tame' analysis situs. There is a set F of 'figures', a set M (cells or pieces), an order ≤ (on p.69 this is subdivision) and a binary relation R, which he calls 'compatibility'. In his formula R actually behaves as disjointness or orthogonality. On p.67 R induces a Galois connection between subsets of F and subsets of M. Each subset has a smallest saturated hull, called its support (resp. cosupport). Saturated parts on the two sides correspond bijectively and inclusion-reversingly. Their common lattice Σ is called the 'virtual supports'. In Σ, arbitrary Inf are intersections and arbitrary Sup are the saturation of the union, so Σ is a complete lattice.

On p.68 he 'presumes' that Σ is in fact a Boolean algebra. It would be 'ultra-stonian', because arbitrary Sups exist, i.e. a complete Boolean algebra. So supports would be identified with the clopen subsets of a spectral, totally disconnected, ultra-stonian space. In modern terms this is the Stone space of a complete Boolean algebra, an extremally disconnected compact space (Stone, Gleason). Complementation is the corresponding involution.

He then shows Σ depends only on the triple (M, ≤, R), not on the full family of subsets of M given by figures. The complement of M' ⊂ M is the polar comp_M(M') = {x ∈ M | (x,x') ∈ R for all x' ∈ M'}. Σ is then the set of bi-polar-closed subsets. This is the standard closure system of an orthogonality space (Birkhoff polarity).

Margin: this will be computed in the 'set-theoretic' case and in the model examples. For the standard example on a set E, Σ identifies with the power set of E (he seems to note the discrete case). There distributivity P∧(Q∨R) = (P∧Q)∨(P∧R) holds for all P, Q, R. The bottom of the page announces examples of 'partitions' M' of M and extremal partitions, 'using (4)', an axiom from an earlier page.

Purpose: build an intrinsic Boolean 'algebra of supports' for the axiomatic tame-topology framework that the following pages refine (C5 onward, the 'modérée' condition).
errors: The Boolean property is only presumed. For an arbitrary symmetric relation R, the bi-polar-closed sets form a complete ortholattice, which need not be distributive (e.g. orthogonality in a Hilbert space gives the non-distributive lattice of closed subspaces). Booleanness needs an extra axiom. One sufficient axiom: R is exactly 'no common lower bound' for an order, with separativity. The bi-polar-closed sets are then the regular open sets, which always form a complete Boolean algebra. Grothendieck checks distributivity only in the set-theoretic example.
Terminology is inconsistent: R is called 'relation de compatibilité', yet the complement formula uses it as a disjointness/orthogonality relation. On p.69 he notes that 'compatible' is 'déjà pris'.

'Ultra-stonien' is non-standard. In the French tradition (Dixmier), 'stonien' means extremally disconnected and 'hyperstonien' is a stronger measure-theoretic notion. Completeness of Σ gives 'stonien', not 'hyperstonien'.

ideas.what: Complete lattice of saturated (bi-polar-closed) subsets from a relation; support/cosupport anti-isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity; closure system of an orthogonality space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (1940); Ore (1944); later formal concept analysis (Wille)

ideas.what: Presumption that the algebra of virtual supports is a complete Boolean algebra, realised as the clopens of an extremally disconnected Stone space
ideas.modern_name: Stone duality for complete Boolean algebras; Stonean (extremally disconnected) spaces

ideas.what: Complement as polar with respect to R; Σ depends only on (M, ≤, R)
ideas.modern_name: Orthocomplement in an orthogonality space; regular-open / Boolean completion of a separative poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Foulis–Randall (orthogonality spaces); Scott, Solovay, Vopěnka (Boolean completion in forcing, 1960s)

missed.claim: In a combinatorial axiomatics of tame topology (figures, subdivision, disjointness), Grothendieck builds an intrinsic complete Boolean algebra of 'virtual supports' and its Stone space. This parallels the Boolean algebra of definable sets and the o-minimal or real spectrum (spectral spaces of types) in later o-minimal tame topology. It also parallels the regular-open Boolean completion used in forcing. The link is implicit and undeveloped.
missed.quote: les supports s'identifient aux parties ouvertes et fermées d'un espace spectral, qui serait un espace tot. discontinu ultra-stonien
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mildly: it shows that the 1986 Analysis situs project aimed at a Stone-dual 'space of virtual points' attached to a tame structure. That is close to Pillay's o-minimal spectrum (1988) and the Coste–Roy real spectrum. But the content here is elementary and only conjectural.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard lattice theory (Galois connections, polars, Stone duality for complete Boolean algebras), stated tentatively and without proof. Its interest is only as a glimpse of how Grothendieck's tame-topology axiomatics was meant to yield a Stone-type space of virtual supports.
